target_customer: Conference attendees and speakers; later companies paying to track conference speaker activity
problem: Finding relevant conferences and the slides, notes and videos from them was scattered across the web.
business_model: Free social directory with a paid Pro tier for businesses tracking speaker activity

founders.name: Simon Willison
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: co-creator of Django and creator of Datasette.

founders.name: Natalie Downe
founders.background_notes: Named as creator in Wikipedia; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Plancast
competitors.what: General purpose event site with Twitter and Facebook sign in

technical_complexity.rationale: A Django web app aggregating Twitter data and user contributions; engineering was standard for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Content accumulated over time, but the data model was copyable by event platforms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Eventbrite bought Lanyrd in September 2013; the site later went read-only and closed, redirecting to Eventbrite.

market_need_then: Conference listings were scattered across general event sites; Lanyrd launched in September 2010 and raised a seed in 2011 on early traction.

branding.name_origin: A play on lanyard, the conference badge holder; Willison also said the domain was available and a made-up word made feedback easy to search.
branding.domain_note: lanyrd.com was available when they chose the name; it now redirects to Eventbrite.
branding.community_and_virality: Strong developer community following; Simon Willison blogged the launch and it was covered by TechCrunch and Zeldman.

brand_strength.rationale: Well liked in web community circles and covered at launch, but no evidence of mainstream reach.

outcome_analysis: Lanyrd was a two person conference directory that launched in September 2010, went through YC in winter 2011, and raised a 1.4 million dollar seed in September 2011 from Index Seed, PROfounders and angels. Eventbrite acquired it in September 2013 at an undisclosed price in its first acquisitions in seven years, after which the product went read-only and closed, so the outcome looks like a team and data acquisition.
notes: lanyrd.com redirects to eventbrite.com (301), so the original site is dead. Funding sourced from TechCrunch via a search summary and cross-checked with Wikipedia ($1.4M, September 2011). Competitors are dated October and November 2010, before the winter 2011 batch.
